[[File:Dungu's Fish Tea shack.jpg|thumb|A fish tea shack at [[Winifred Beach]] in [[Port Antonio]], [[Jamaica]]]]

'''Fish tea''' is a spicy soup in [[Caribbean cuisine]] and [[Jamaican cuisine]]. It is similar to a fish [[bouillon (broth)|bouillon]] and can take several hours to prepare. It includes ground [[Yam (vegetable)|yam]], [[pumpkin]], [[cassava]], [[potatoes]] and green bananas, cooked until very soft. As much as 15 pounds of fish is added to make five gallons.<ref name="cookoff">[http://www.caycompass.com/cgi-bin/CFPnews.cgi?ID=1010216 Fish Tea Cookoff a big part of East End Surf Challenge] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728062405/http://www.caycompass.com/cgi-bin/CFPnews.cgi?ID=1010216 |date=28 July 2011 }} 10 January 2006 Camanian Compass</ref> Carrots and [[cho–cho]] can also be added. It is flavored with [[coconut milk]] and seasoned with various ingredients that may include black pepper, salt, thyme,  butter, scallion and season–all."<ref name="cookoff"/><ref name="tea">Alan Ebanks [http://www.caycompass.com/cgi-bin/CFPnews.cgi?ID=1036703  Surfers find it tea–licious] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728062440/http://www.caycompass.com/cgi-bin/CFPnews.cgi?ID=1036703 |date=28 July 2011 }} 13 January 2009 Cay Compass</ref>

Fish tea is similar to traditional [[run down]], but instead of chunks the ingredients are boiled until they are in a "soupy liquid form".<ref name="cookoff"/> Some believe it to be an [[aphrodisiac]] and it is associated with various legends and rumors:

*"If you drink that fish tea, you’ll have to chain yourself to the bed post at night or else you’ll walk all night" (in search of adventure)<ref name="cookoff"/><ref name="tea"/>
*"Men who haven’t fathered children all of a sudden produced twins"
*"Once you take that fish tea you won't be able to walk a straight line."<ref name="cookoff"/>
According to a [[Cayman Islands]] publication "those who taste the fish tea always seem to come back for more."<ref name="cookoff"/>
